integrated_description: The artist immediately names the racial exclusivity condition as an ethical boundary, then offers a single structured negotiation: clarifying whether the client seeks traditional style versus racial essentialism, and proposing a concrete alternative that preserves traditional aesthetic while depicting the sitter's actual identity without racial templating. If the client refuses to remove the racial exclusivity condition after this one negotiation attempt, the artist declines the commission outright, ensuring no prolonged dialogue normalizes discriminatory constraints as adjustable preferences.
integration_rationale: All three modifications converge on the same two-stage structure — explicit upfront boundary-setting followed by a single negotiation attempt and a hard refusal if the exclusionary condition persists — making full integration achievable without tension. The concrete alternative (sitter's real identity in traditional style) and the one-attempt limit satisfy stakeholder_a's structure, stakeholder_b's anti-normalization concern, and stakeholder_c's explicit fallback requirement simultaneously.
